title: Roots and Elicitation — Scoping and Mid-Flight User Input

questions.question: A helper is told to delete an item by name, but three items share that name. What should it do?
options: Delete all three to be safe
Pick the oldest one without asking
Pretend it succeeded and change nothing
Stop and ask which one is meant before touching anything
questions.explanation: Ambiguous destructive actions must pause for the user. This lesson builds the two guards: roots that bound where a server may act, and elicitation that asks mid-flight.

questions.question: What interaction occurs when deleting the three TPS notes?
options: The tool deletes all three without asking
elicitation picks note-14 and confirm=true
It rejects every multi-match request as ambiguous
It reads a prompt but never changes the notes
questions.explanation: Multiple matches trigger structured elicitation; the fixture chooses note-14 and confirm true, so that in-root note is removed.

questions.question: What happens to the unambiguous shopping note?
options: It is held for manual review
It is copied to Scratch
It deletes the in-root shopping note
It triggers an OAuth step-up
questions.explanation: A single matching note still passes the root check, so notes_delete deletes the shopping note without a multi-choice prompt.

questions.question: What result does deleting the outside-root target produce?
options: A successful deletion because the title is unique
A new root is automatically granted
A prompt that moves it into Notes
outside-roots error
questions.explanation: The tool checks the note URI against ROOTS before deletion and refuses the /tmp target even when there is only one match.

questions.question: What does tool_notes_setup do in URL elicitation mode when the fixture accepts?
options: setup complete
It deletes the Notes root
It returns setup cancelled without showing a URL
It treats the URL as a note id
questions.explanation: URL mode shows the browser-based setup interaction; the accepted FAKE_USER_ANSWERS entry produces the setup complete result.

questions.question: What should a server do after ROOTS.pop removes the Scratch root?
options: Continue using every previously granted path forever
drop handles outside new roots
Turn all file URIs into HTTP URLs
Delete every note in the remaining Notes root
questions.explanation: Root changes narrow the client's authorization boundary, so the demo notes that the server must drop handles outside the new roots.
